why: Inserting the core-principle blocked cuts that split predicates/arguments and enumerations, so the scorer stopped keeping many short internal splits (improving the smallest latency bins ≤3 and ≤5). However the constraint caused the kept-cut budget to be reallocated in mid-length pieces (bins ≤7 and ≤10), producing more cuts that split subjects/verbs or other heads and so made many mid-length cases worse.
lesson: A later revision should preserve the benefit of preventing internal predicate/argument and enumeration splits for short pieces while avoiding wholesale reallocation of cuts that creates new subject–verb or head splits in mid-length examples.
